question: Which four elements form the main building blocks of most nutrients in our diet?
explanation: Spot on! These four simple elements form the chemical backbone of the carbohydrates, fats, proteins, and nucleic acids we eat every day. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to understand the basic chemistry of food nutrients?

options.A: It determines the physical weight and height requirements for clinical admissions
options.B: It explains how the body transforms food into cellular fuel and structural components
options.C: It allows nurses to calculate exact retail food prices for hospital kitchens
options.D: It helps nurses prescribe specific synthetic chemical medications for patients

explanation: Knowing how nutrients are built helps you understand digestion and why our bodies need a mix of different foods to stay healthy. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h1)

question: What do we call single-ring sugar molecules like glucose and fructose?
explanation: You got it! 'Mono' means single, and 'saccharide' means sugar, making monosaccharides the simplest form of carbohydrate. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h2)

question: When a patient eats a complex starch, what must happen before the body can absorb it?

options.A: It must gain extra nitrogen atoms to form a protein chain
options.B: It must be transformed into a mineral salt solution
options.C: It must be broken down into single monosaccharide rings
options.D: It must be converted directly into a complex lipid structure

explanation: Your gut can only absorb tiny, single sugar units. That is why large starches must be broken down by digestion first! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h2)

question: What is the typical chemical structure of a dietary fat (triglyceride)?

options.A: Four interlocking carbon rings with a side chain
options.B: One nitrogen group attached to a central carbon ring
options.C: Two sugar rings joined by a strong glycosidic bond
options.D: One glycerol molecule attached to three fatty acid tails

explanation: Think of it like a central backbone (glycerol) holding onto three fatty acid tails—hence 'tri-glyceride'. Great job! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h3)

question: What makes a saturated fatty acid different from an unsaturated fatty acid?

options.A: Saturated fats lack any hydrogen atoms along the carbon chain
options.B: Saturated fats contain only single carbon-to-carbon bonds
options.C: Saturated fats contain multiple carbon-to-carbon double bonds
options.D: Saturated fats always dissolve easily in plain water

explanation: Because they only have single bonds, saturated fat molecules pack tightly together, which is why they are usually solid at room temperature. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h3)

question: Which chemical element is found in proteins (amino acids) but is generally absent in pure carbs and fats?
explanation: Spot on! Every amino acid contains a special amine group made of nitrogen, setting proteins apart from carbs and fats. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h4)

question: What happens to a protein's structure when it is exposed to high heat (denaturation)?

options.A: Its three-dimensional folded shape unfolds and loses function
options.B: It transforms instantly into a simple carbohydrate molecule
options.C: Its individual amino acids permanently vanish into gas
options.D: It gains extra carbon atoms to become a saturated lipid

explanation: Heat breaks the delicate bonds holding the protein's shape together, making it unfold and stop working (like frying an egg!). [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h4)

question: Why do water-soluble vitamins dissolve easily in our blood?

options.A: They are built from long chains of saturated fatty acids
options.B: They consist entirely of interlocking cholesterol rings
options.C: Their chemical structures contain many polar groups
options.D: They contain heavy mineral salt deposits

explanation: Like dissolves like! Polar parts of the vitamin love interacting with water, allowing them to travel smoothly through the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h5)

question: A patient who cannot digest fats properly is most at risk of lacking which group of vitamins?

options.B: Vitamins A, D, E, and K

explanation: You've got this! Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble, meaning they hitch a ride with fats to be absorbed by your gut. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h5)

question: What is the main chemical difference between vitamins and minerals?

options.A: Vitamins contain heavy metal ions instead of carbon
options.B: Minerals are fragile organic compounds destroyed by cooking
options.C: Minerals are inorganic elements that lack carbon-hydrogen bonds
options.D: Vitamins are solid metallic rocks found naturally in soil

explanation: Correct! Minerals are pure elemental substances from the earth, while vitamins are complex organic molecules made by living things. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h6)

question: Why can boiling vegetables destroy certain vitamins while leaving the minerals mostly untouched?

options.A: Minerals are stable inorganic elements that cannot be broken down by heat
options.B: Vitamins are protected by tough outer shells that boiling water cracks
options.C: Minerals evaporate into steam immediately when exposed to warm water
options.D: Vitamins have strong metallic bonds that prevent them from dissolving

explanation: Because minerals are simple elements rather than fragile organic structures, cooking heat cannot break them apart. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h6)

question: What makes water a polar molecule?

options.A: An unequal sharing of electrical charge between hydrogen and oxygen atoms
options.B: A complete absence of chemical bonds between its constituent atoms
options.C: An equal balance of heavy metal ions dissolved in its liquid state
options.D: The presence of long carbon chains running through its core

explanation: The oxygen atom pulls electrons closer to itself, giving water a slightly negative side and a slightly positive hydrogen side. Clever design! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h7)

question: How does water's polarity help keep our bodies running?

options.A: It provides a dense source of stored glucose calories for hard work
options.B: It builds rigid structural amino acid chains inside human bone
options.C: It acts as a universal solvent that dissolves and transports vital nutrients
options.D: It prevents minerals from entering the bloodstream during digestion

explanation: Because water is polar, it easily dissolves and carries important chemicals and nutrients to every part of the body. Excellent! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h7)
